title: BASIC# Tokenizer and Reader Implementation Under Ruby Referee
purpose: Begin the first BASIC# tokenizer/reader implementation while keeping the Ruby bootstrap lexer as the reference referee.

allowed: implementing compiler/tokenizer_reader.rb as a deterministic reader/token-record producer
comparing BASIC# tokenizer/reader reader records against the existing Ruby Lexer referee
locking line numbers, raw line text, trimmed text, comment handling, block body boundaries, and current Head detection
adding executable implementation fixtures for head, Body, result marker, action word, and quoted text token records
preserving current Ruby parser, runtime, BSharp IR, BSharp Bytecode, Save, ASK, and input-device behavior
forbidden_until_later_approval: replacing compiler/lexer.rb or compiler/parser.rb as the authority
routing the production parser through compiler/tokenizer_reader.rb
adding loops, functions, reusable words, collections, interpolation, or multiline text
changing runtime meaning, BSharp IR, BSharp Bytecode, Save format, ASK output, input devices, graphics, engine bridge, browser work, web export, or Ruby retirement

reader_record_schema.number: one-based source line number after comment preservation
reader_record_schema.raw: comment-stripped source line with original non-comment characters and without trailing newline
reader_record_schema.text: raw line trimmed at both ends; blank lines are omitted

comment_rules: // opens a BASIC# block comment when outside a quoted text value
/. closes a BASIC# block comment when outside a quoted text value
commented characters are replaced by spaces so later column positions remain stable
// and /. inside quoted text values are ordinary text
a comment closing marker without an open comment produces a reader issue
a nested comment opening marker produces a reader issue
an unclosed comment produces a reader issue pointing at the opening position

future_token_record_schema.kind: head, body_open, body_close, body_line, result_line, action_word, quoted_text, comment_issue, or diagnostic_anchor
future_token_record_schema.column: one-based source column where the token begins after comment preservation
future_token_record_schema.text: exact creator-facing text for the token
future_token_record_schema.normalized: canonical comparison form only when an existing accepted rule already defines one

acceptance_rules: The tokenizer/reader contract tool must pass in the Trial-by-Fire validation inventory.
compiler/tokenizer_reader.rb must produce reader records equal to the Ruby Lexer referee for every contract fixture.
The implementation must not be used as the production parser authority until a later approved build.
The contract must not change Profiles 1 through 7, BSharp Bytecode Profiles 1 through 7, Save format, runtime behavior, ASK behavior, or input meaning.
Ruby remains the bootstrap compiler and reference referee until BASIC# compiler pieces reproduce approved output deterministically.

implementation_record_schema.reader_records: deterministic records that must equal the Ruby Lexer referee line records
implementation_record_schema.token_records: deterministic future-facing token records generated from accepted reader records
implementation_record_schema.issues: comment and reader issues mirrored from the Ruby Lexer referee
